### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Question

Not sure if this is a me-thing, so figured I would raise this as a discussion/Q&A first.

But I've noticed with `mini.completion`, the completion list is never accurate when I'm first typing for something.  So I have to exit from insert to normal, go back in, and continue trying to complete what I'm looking for to get an accurate list.

It's sort of hard to explain, and not sure if this is an LSP server matter, but I struggle to lean towards that since it works accurately first-time around with `nvim-cmp`.

My `mini.completion` set up is pretty plain Jane:

```lua
require("mini.completion").setup({
    lsp_completion = {
        source_func = "omnifunc",
    },
})
```

I've also noticed this is only really happening for one LSP.  But it's the same LSP I've used before when I was using NvChad.  Which I've been migrating things away from because I got exhausted from dealing with the abstractions NvChad was doing.

Here is [one of the examples](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1230#issue-2534614552) (the "Steps to reproduce" section) of what would help very much here.

I plan to take a closer look in the upcoming 'mini.completion' updates, but making it work is somewhat problematic.

The reason here is because 'mini.completion' deliberately uses Neovim's built-in 'omnifunc'/'completefunc' mechanism to filter down candidates once it received response from LSP server(s). As far as I understand the LSP specification, respecting `isIncomplete` would require to somehow interject into that order of things, which doesn't look straightforward.

I'll take a closer look here to confirm this in case I'll be able to reproduce the behavior.

reply_data.bodyHTML:
Yes, I am not really familiar with PHP and thus need a step-by-step guidance in order to reproduce the issue. Without actually reproducing it there are very limited ways to help. Here is #1230 (comment) (the "Steps to reproduce" section) of what would help very much here.

I need to make some assumptions, namely you're using Ubuntu though the general premise applies to Mac or other Linux distros as well. But as that is what I use in WSL, I need to approach it from that:

  • Install PHP & Composer: sudo apt install php-cli composer
  • Install Node & Intelephense (free version should suffice): sudo apt install nodejs npm && npm install -g intelephense
  • You should be able to run intelephense and get an error about input stream not set (expected): intelephense
  • Create a folder (this will assume /tmp/phptest moving forward) and cd into it
  • Run composer require illuminate/support
  • Have mini.completion & lsp configured in Neovim, and configured to use intelephense (see lua config below)
  • Create a new PHP file in Neovim:
<?php

class A {
  public function b()
  {
    // cursor here
  }
}

In the script above, remove the // line and type $var = new Collect, and you won't see the expected value of Illuminate\Support\Collection, but when you do <C-Space> the list will refresh and the expected item will exist.

Lua config (this can probably be modified but it's mimicking what I have with most fluff stripped out):

local config = {
    lsp = {
        ["intelephense"] = {},
    },
}

local lspconfig = require("lspconfig")

local on_attach = function(_, bufnr)
end

local common_capabilities = function(server)
    local capabilities = vim.lsp.protocol.make_client_capabilities()
    capabilities.textDocument.completion.completionItem.snippetSupport = false
    return capabilities
end

for server, opts in pairs(config.lsp) do
    local lsp_opts = {
        on_attach = on_attach,
        capabilities = common_capabilities(server),
    }

    lspconfig[server].setup(lsp_opts)
end

require("mini.completion").setup({
    lsp_completion = {
        source_func = "omnifunc",
    },
})

I'm not sure if there's anything else you would need, but this is what I can think of.

Follow up question

I was reading through the source but couldn't find an answer to this. Since the two-step result works for what I need, is there a way to force this to happen instead of whatever happens the first time, whether by language or globally?

> I was reading through the source but couldn't find an answer to this. Since the two-step result works for what I need, is there a way to force this to happen instead of whatever happens the first time, whether by language or globally?

If by "two-step" you mean the "get autocompletion, type something, press `<C-Space>`", then I don't think so. The whole premise of the `isIncomplete` (which is the most probable assumption at the moment) is that it is just the way LSP server responds at the particular context. So if autocompletion doesn't return all results, then forcing it in the same context with `<C-Space>` won't help.

> I can, but I don't have the whole mini.nvim suite installed currently. Since this is specific to completion (**I think**) can the branch be pushed also to the https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.completion repo? If not I understand.

Sure, I've pushed the [`isincomplete`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.completion/tree/isincomplete) branch to a standalone repo.

I also opted out of triggering completion immediately for trigger characters; only retriggering after incomplete previous list is immediate. As per LSP spec, those are meant to have the same nature as regular "identifier characters" (usually `[a-zA-Z]`, but in Neovim it is controlled by 'iskeyword' option), just specific to the language itself (like `.`, `$`, etc.).

Just a heads up:
- I was able to reproduce the original "missing items; need to <C-Space>" issue in a bigger project. It is indeed caused by `isIncomplete` and the pushed branches should indeed fix that.
- There is currently visible flickering (popup menu disappears and reappears in very quick succession) for when 'mini.completion' tries to force update the list after `isIncomplete`. I *think* I have a solution, though.

As these changes are probably going to be merged into `main` anyway, confirming the above findings is not a high priority. If you're busy, you can wait until those are merged with a cleaner implementation.

  • I was able to reproduce the original "missing items; need to " issue in a bigger project. It is indeed caused by isIncomplete and the pushed branches should indeed fix that.
  • There is currently visible flickering (popup menu disappears and reappears in very quick succession) for when 'mini.completion' tries to force update the list after isIncomplete. I think I have a solution, though.

As these changes are probably going to be merged into main anyway, confirming the above findings is not a high priority. If you're busy, you can wait until those are merged with a cleaner implementation.
